title: 2026 U.S. Senate election in Kentucky
description: Kentucky will elect one member to the U.S. Senate in 2026 for the open Class III seat formerly held by Mitch McConnell, who announced in February 2025 that he would not seek re-election. The race matters because it will help determine control of the U.S. Senate, and Kentucky remains a strongly Republican state in federal elections. Republicans are contesting a crowded primary featuring figures such as Andy Barr and Daniel Cameron, while Democrats have a multi-candidate field led in early polling by Charles Booker. The general election is expected to test whether Democrats can make the race competitive in a state that has not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1992.

candidates.name: Andy Barr
candidates.summary: Andy Barr is a Republican U.S. representative from Kentucky’s 6th Congressional District and a candidate for the U.S. Senate in Kentucky in 2026. He has served in Congress since 2013 and is running on a conservative platform that emphasizes border security, tax cuts, energy production, and opposition to DEI programs.

Healthcare.stance: Barr says he supports expanding access to affordable health care while reducing bureaucratic barriers between patients and doctors. His campaign and congressional site also highlight support for community health centers, medical research, Medicare payment reforms, and faster coverage decisions for innovative medical devices.

Economy.stance: Barr supports extending the Trump-era tax cuts, reducing federal spending, and lowering the national debt. He frames these policies as pro-growth measures intended to support wages, investment, and Kentucky businesses.

Climate/Energy.stance: Barr supports expanding domestic energy production, especially coal and fossil fuels, and opposes Biden-era energy regulations and the Green New Deal. His campaign says he favors expedited permitting and policies aimed at restoring Kentucky coal jobs and energy dominance.

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Barr describes himself as pro-life. He supports the Hyde Amendment and the Born Alive Protection Act, opposes taxpayer funding for abortion, and says he supported overturning Roe v. Wade.

Immigration.stance: Barr supports stricter immigration enforcement, including border security, deporting undocumented immigrants, restarting border wall construction, and ending catch-and-release policies. His campaign also says he supports more border agents and stronger federal enforcement.

sources.title: Issues | Andy Barr for Senate

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Barr says he strongly supports Second Amendment rights and opposes gun-control measures that he says would burden law-abiding gun owners. His campaign highlights endorsements from the NRA and Gun Owners of America and says he received an A+ rating from the NSSF.

Foreign Policy.stance: Barr focuses on countering the Chinese Communist Party and limiting U.S. capital from flowing to Chinese military, surveillance, and technology companies. He supports sanctions and investment restrictions and says he has backed legislation such as the FIGHT China Act and COINS Act.

candidates.summary: Charles Booker is a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate and a former Kentucky state representative. His campaign has focused on economic fairness, health care, and opposition to concentrated political and corporate power.

Economy.stance: Charles Booker’s economy plan centers on a workers-first agenda: the 40x40x45 framework guarantees full-time workers at least $45,000 per year and 40 hours of paid sick leave, funded by a wealth tax and closing loopholes. He also advocates universal basic income, universal childcare, affordable housing, stronger unions, debt relief, and strategic public investment in infrastructure, alongside anti-monopoly reforms and protections for workers in the AI era.

Immigration.stance: Charles Booker supports abolishing ICE and replacing it with a humane immigration enforcement system that prioritizes due process, accountability, and community safety; he would end ICE funding and dismantle the agency. Foreign Policy.stance: Charles Booker advocates for a pro-peace, pro-humanitarian approach in U.S. foreign policy. He has framed U.S. policy toward Gaza as requiring a humanitarian-focused solution, supports a free Palestine, calls for an end to funding the violence in Gaza, and emphasizes prioritizing human rights and de-escalation while opposing unconditional arms support to foreign governments. He argues for accountability and a reevaluation of U.S. funding abroad to prioritize civilian protection and human rights.

sources.title: Issues - Charles Booker For U.S. Senate 2026

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Charles Booker supports robust federal civil rights protections, including strong LGBTQ equality safeguards, and will advocate for anti-discrimination measures to ensure equal rights and dignity for all people. He also opposes efforts to roll back civil rights protections and will push federal policies that safeguard marginalized communities.

sources.title: Issues - Charles Booker For U.S. Senate 2026

Education.stance: Charles Booker supports fully funded public education with full and equitable investment in Kentucky's education system, ensuring that every Kentucky child has the resources, facilities, and opportunities to pursue their dreams.

Tech & AI.stance: Charles Booker supports strong guardrails for AI development and an immediate moratorium on new AI data centers until environmental, community, and worker protections are in place. He also advocates for sharing AI-derived value with workers through a public equity stake, prohibiting AI-only hiring/firing decisions, a federal jobs guarantee with retraining, and establishing a Human Labor Protection Bureau to enforce these protections.

reviews.summary: This is a well-constructed, factually accurate profile of the 2026 Kentucky U.S. Senate race with strong sourcing across all major candidates. The profile demonstrates excellent coverage of Republican primary (Barr, Cameron, Morris) and Democratic primary (Booker, McGrath, and three secondary candidates) with high-confidence issue positions backed by official campaign sites, credible news outlets, and government sources. Candidate backgrounds are consistently documented with education and career history sourced appropriately. Language is neutral and nonpartisan across nearly all issue summaries. Polling data is dated and sourced. The agent appropriately marked low-confidence stances for lesser-known candidates (Blanton, Thompson, Forsythe) as 'no public position found' rather than inventing positions, reflecting good-faith research discipline. Minor issues are noted below, but none rise to the level of requiring a revision before publication.

The summary references the 'Make America Healthy Again' agenda, which is a recent political movement. Ensure this is attributed directly to the candidate's campaign materials to distinguish it from broader political trends.

The description states Mitch McConnell announced his decision not to seek re-election in 'February 2025'. While the profile treats this as ground truth, ensure this aligns with the timeline of the provided research sources.

reviews.summary: Strong, well-sourced profile with consistent internal sourcing across major candidates. Andy Barr, Daniel Cameron, Charles Booker, and Amy McGrath have detailed issue positions backed by direct campaign sites, official congressional pages, and credible news outlets. Backgrounds and career histories align with cited sources. Minor candidates show appropriate transparency about limited public information. Language is largely neutral with only isolated stylistic issues.

validation_grade.summary: Validated by 3/3 reviewers with an average score of 91/100.

forecast.rationale: The available numeric polling only covers the Republican primary, where Andy Barr leads but the GOP nomination remains unsettled. There is no general-election head-to-head polling in the provided data, so uncertainty is meaningful. Still, the race description states Kentucky remains a strongly Republican state in federal elections and notes Democrats have not won a U.S. Senate race there since 1992. In an open-seat contest, that partisan baseline strongly favors whichever Republican emerges, though the lack of general-election polling and the unsettled primary argue against a safe rating at this stage.
